description: Given a triangle array, return the minimum path sum from top to bottom. For each step, you may move to an adjacent number of the row below. Adjacent means index i or i+1 in the next row.
intuition: Start from the bottom of the triangle and work upward. For each cell, replace it with its value plus the minimum of its two children below. When you reach the top, the apex contains the minimum path sum. Bottom-up avoids the need for backtracking.
approach: Use bottom-up DP. Start from the bottom row and work upward. For each cell, the minimum path sum is the cell value plus the minimum of its two children below. Modify the triangle in place or use a 1D array.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: triangle = [[2],[3,4],[6,5,7],[4,1,8,3]]

Start with bottom row: dp = [4, 1, 8, 3]

i=2 (row [6,5,7]):
  j=0: currentCell=6, bestBelow=min(dp[0],dp[1])=min(4,1)=1 -> dp[0]=6+1=7
  j=1: currentCell=5, bestBelow=min(dp[1],dp[2])=min(1,8)=1 -> dp[1]=5+1=6
  j=2: currentCell=7, bestBelow=min(dp[2],dp[3])=min(8,3)=3 -> dp[2]=7+3=10
  dp = [7, 6, 10, 3]

i=1 (row [3,4]):
  j=0: currentCell=3, bestBelow=min(7,6)=6 -> dp[0]=3+6=9
  j=1: currentCell=4, bestBelow=min(6,10)=6 -> dp[1]=4+6=10
  dp = [9, 10, 10, 3]

i=0 (row [2]):
  j=0: currentCell=2, bestBelow=min(9,10)=9 -> dp[0]=2+9=11
  dp = [11, ...]

Output: dp[0] = 11 (path: 2->3->5->1)
explanation:
1. Start with the bottom row as the initial DP array.
2. Work upward: for each cell, add the minimum of its two children.
3. dp[j] = triangle[i][j] + min(dp[j], dp[j+1]).
4. After processing all rows, dp[0] contains the minimum path sum.
5. Bottom-up approach avoids complex indexing of top-down.
hints: Bottom-up DP is simpler than top-down for this problem.
Start from the last row and propagate minimums upward.
Each cell depends on two cells in the row below.
